newsitem.title: USA: Widow of Malcolm X dies after fire.
newsitem.headline: Widow of Malcolm X dies after fire.

text.p: The widow of slain U.S. civil rights leader Malcolm X died on Monday from severe burns suffered in a fire allegedly set by her grandson.
Betty Shabazz, 63, who became an educator and human rights activist after her husband's murder, died at a New York hospital with family members at her side, a hospital spokeswoman said.
She suffered burns on more than 80 percent of her body as she struggled to put out the fire in her Yonkers, New York, apartment just after midnight on June 1.
Police said her troubled 12-year-old grandson Malcolm, named after his grandfather, started the fire.
New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani announced her death at City Hall.

"I'm sure all the people of the city of New York join me in offering our condolences and sympathy and prayers and our support for the family which is going through such a difficult time," Giuliani said.
Malcolm X was murdered at the Audubon Ballroom in Manhattan on February 21, 1965.
Shabazz was sitting in the audience with her four young daughters when he was gunned down. She had twin girls after his death.
One of the daughters who witnessed the murder was Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, then four years old.
In 1995, she was indicted on charges of plotting to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, whom her mother had accused of playing a role in her husband's assassination.
Malcolm X had been Farrakhan's spiritual mentor and for many years the right-hand man and heir apparent to Elijah Muhammad, head of the Nation of Islam.
The federal case against Qubilah Shabazz was dropped after she completed two years of counselling.
It was her son who is accused of setting the fatal fire. He was staying with his grandmother while his mother sorted out personal problems.
After the death of her husband, Shabazz earned a doctorate in education. Most recently, she was a public relations administrator at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn, New York.

She also became a champion for human rights, participating in the United States Aid for International Development Conference in South Africa and travelling extensively in Africa, Europe and the Caribbean.
